text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition parliamentarians file a suit seeking to bar parliament from debating last Thursday's 1997/98 budget speech.

- Attorney General Amos Wako orders the re-opening of the Goldenberg file, a 5.8 billion ($105.4 million) scandal involving former senior central bank officials and prominent businessman Kamlesh Pattni.
- The Electoral Commission says at least six million people registered as voters by last Sunday.
- Fifty opposition members of parliament say they held a secret meeting to chart out a strategy to disrupt the presentation of the budget proposals in parliament last week.
- President Daniel arap Moi criticises the clergy for using the pulpit for politics.
- Voter registration centres complain they cannot cope with a last minute rush to beat Tuesday's registration deadline saying they have run out of stationery.
- The Social Democratic Party declares its support for presidential hopeful Charity Ngilu.
